relations.myth: Living Apis manifests and communicates Ptah’s presence
relations.note: Apis is Ptah’s herald, ba, and living manifestation at Memphis.
Apis receives priestly and royal care as Ptah’s sacred manifestation.
Every deceased Apis is ritually united with Osiris as Osiris-Apis.

relations.myth: Osiris’s soul enters successive Apis bulls
relations.note: Osiris’s soul reportedly passes into Apis and then each successor.
Plutarch describes living Apis as the animate image of Osiris.
Isis is identified with the divine mother of the Apis bull.

relations.myth: Isis places Osiris’s remains in wooden ox
relations.note: Isis encloses Osiris’s remains in a linen-covered wooden ox explaining bovine reverence.
Some contexts associate Apis’s divine mother with Hathoric forms.
Some authorities reportedly regarded the Heliopolitan sacred bull as Apis’s sire.
Apis’s solar disk and uraeus assimilate him to royal-solar potency.

relations.myth: Late Memphite and solar theological combinations
relations.note: Apis occurs with Atum in theological combinations without an independent narrative encounter.
Anubian funerary functions operate within Apis’s embalming and burial rites.
relations.source: Late ritual texts and Saqqara installations

relations.note: Serapeum dedications invoke Thoth alongside the transfigured Osiris-Apis.
Horus appears in Apis burial decoration and funerary theology.
The Sons of Horus occur in Apis burial decoration and embalming theology.
Osiris-Apis supplied Sarapis’s name and theological base before broader Hellenistic development.
relations.source: Curse of Artemisia and later tradition

relations.note: Through Sarapis, Apis’s Hellenistic derivative was equated with the underworld ruler.
Sarapis, derived from Osiris-Apis, absorbed Zeus’s sovereign functions.
Sarapis, derived from Osiris-Apis, was functionally equated with Helios.
Sarapis, derived from Osiris-Apis, was functionally combined with Dionysus.
Sarapis, derived from Osiris-Apis, absorbed healing functions associated with Asclepius.
Herodotus identifies the Egyptian Apis with the Greek divine bull Epaphos.
